chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: If a man commits adultery with his father's wife or his father's slave girl, that does not prohibit her from her husband, nor does the slave girl become prohibited to her master. That prohibition from him occurs only when he has intercourse with the slave girl while she is permissible to him; thus, that slave girl becomes permanently prohibited to his father and to his son. And if a man marries a woman with a valid marriage, the woman becomes prohibited to his father and to his son.

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَلَا لِابْنِهِ: to his father and to his son

ai.seo_question: Does adultery with a father's wife prohibit her from her husband?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (AS) clarifies the distinction between *illat al-gharar* (prohibition due to mixture) and *illat al-'aqd* (prohibition due to contract) in the context of vertical kinship. He establishes that while adultery does not permanently bar a slave girl from her master or her husband, lawful intercourse by the father creates a permanent prohibition for the son, whereas a valid marriage contract prohibits the woman to both father and son regardless of consummation. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the effects of *nikah* (contract) and *jima'* (intercourse) on lineage and marital eligibility.
